footnotes: 1 The author writes ‘et’, which would seem to stand for the ‘et-Zeichen’, i.e. ampersand.

2 This word is corrected and it seems the most likely reading is ‘for’ (which equates to ‘vor’ in this author’s spelling), although there are at least the remains of another letter visible before the f.
3 All printed text is rendered in italic. The number 1517 is stamped below the sender’s name.
4 End of address obscured by postage stamp – 67/14 is to be expected based on other postcards.

5 This side of the card is stamped with a postmark reading ‘WIEN 20 | 19.7.40.-12 | d’ and has stamps attached reading ‘Deutsches Reich’ and ‘MIT LUFTP[OST] | PAR AVIO[N]’. The stamp on the left-hand side is somewhat blurred but likely reads ‘Geprüft [?] | Oberkommando der Wehrmacht’.
6 This could possibly be ‘im’ for ‘im[mer] noch’.
7 Several words blotted out with black ink over three lines.
8 End of line obscured by postage stamp – this would most likely have read ‘Grüße’.
9 Possibly just a deletion – the author may have started to write ‘auch’ before continuing along the top edge of the card instead.
